kernelIdea: A ⊆ S means every element of A is in S. To prove it, take an arbitrary x ∈ A and show x ∈ S. ∅ is a subset of everything (vacuously). Subset is transitive.

kernels.l1: A little box is inside a big box when every single thing in the little one is also in the big one.
kernels.l2: One box is part of another when everything in the first box is also in the second. To check, take any one thing from the little box and follow it into the big box. An empty box is part of every box.
kernels.l3: One collection sits inside another when everything in the first is also in the second. To show it, take any one thing from the first and follow it into the second.
kernels.l4: One set is contained in another when every element of the first is an element of the second. The proof method is element chasing: take an arbitrary element of the first and follow it into the second.
kernels.l5: Containment is a conditional claimed about every element, so its proof is an arbitrary-element argument. The empty set is contained in everything, vacuously, and containment is transitive.
kernels.l6: Containment says every element of the first set lies in the second — a conditional claimed about every element. Element chasing is the technique that dictates, and containment partially orders any collection of sets.
kernels.l7: Containment says every element of one set lies in the other, so proving it means taking an arbitrary element of the first and following it into the second. Vacuous truth puts the empty set inside everything, and containment is a partial order.
kernels.l8: ⊆ is the partial order underlying the Boolean algebra of subsets; element chasing is the proof technique that all of naive set theory reduces to, and ∅ ⊆ S is vacuous truth in action.
